info.title: groundhog: give a local app a public HTTPS address through Groundhog.
info.description: The groundhog command: give a local dev server a public HTTPS address through Groundhog.

options.name: --min-duration
options.description:
Saved profiles remember a tunnel name, its local target and its visitor access options, so
host <profile> and start <profile> need no other options. Profiles never store connection keys
or API keys (only --api-key-env names); the connection key comes from GROUNDHOG_KEY, --key, or
the key saved when you created the tunnel, added a key or rotated it here.
host, start, restart and init find groundhog.json in this directory or a parent.
Explicit options override the same-name saved profile, which overrides the project file.
Status and traffic commands describe local sessions; history retains the last 1,000 requests.
--no-interactive (disable menus), --no-color (disable colors; also NO_COLOR),
--no-update-check (skip the periodic update offer; also GROUNDHOG_NO_UPDATE_CHECK=1).
Options for host:
<name>           The tunnel's name, for example myapp.

options.name: --port
options.description: The local port to forward to (http://localhost:<port>).

options.name: --target
options.description: An HTTP or HTTPS local target, for example https://localhost:7132.

options.name: --local-ca
options.description: --insecure-local Skip local certificate validation for loopback HTTPS only (unsafe).

options.name: --key
options.description:
The tunnel's connection key. Prefer the GROUNDHOG_KEY environment variable,
which keeps the key out of your shell history and process list.

options.name: --pool
options.description: Connections to keep open to the relay, 1 to 8 (default 2).

options.name: --verbose
options.description:
Print one line per request.
Visitor access (who may reach the public address; leave out to keep the tunnel's current rules):

options.name: --allow
options.description: Default rule: anyone, or any of members, apikeys, ips joined by commas.

options.name: --ip
options.description: An IP range for ips, for example 203.0.113.0/24. Repeatable.

options.name: --api-key-env
options.description:
An environment variable holding an API key for apikeys (not the
connection key). Repeatable. Only its SHA-256 hash is sent.

options.name: --access-file
options.description:
The rules as JSON ({"default":{"allow":[...]},"rules":[...],"ipRanges":[...]})
instead of --allow, --path and --ip.
Connection keys: a tunnel has at most 2 live keys. key add makes a second key without disconnecting
anything; key revoke <name> <key-id> revokes one key (key list shows the IDs) and disconnects only the
agents using it. key rotate and key revoke <name> replace or revoke every key and disconnect all agents.
User secrets (create, key add, key rotate and key copy), for an Aspire AppHost that reads the tunnel from parameters:

options.name: --project
options.description: The AppHost's .csproj. Writes Parameters:groundhog-tunnel-name (the tunnel name)

options.name: --name-parameter
options.description: Use Parameters:<name> for the tunnel name instead of groundhog-tunnel-name.

options.name: --key-parameter
options.description:
Use Parameters:<name> for the connection key instead of groundhog-tunnel-key.
Exit codes: 0 stopped (Ctrl+C), 1 other failure, 2 bad arguments, 3 key rejected or unknown tunnel.

options.name: --ip
options.description: An IP range for ips, for example 203.0.113.0/24. Repeatable.

options.name: --api-key-env
options.description:
An environment variable holding an API key for apikeys (not the
connection key). Repeatable. Only its SHA-256 hash is sent.

options.name: --access-file
options.description:
The rules as JSON ({"default":{"allow":[...]},"rules":[...],"ipRanges":[...]})
instead of --allow, --path and --ip.
Connection keys: a tunnel has at most 2 live keys. key add makes a second key without disconnecting
anything; key revoke <name> <key-id> revokes one key (key list shows the IDs) and disconnects only the
agents using it. key rotate and key revoke <name> replace or revoke every key and disconnect all agents.
User secrets (create, key add, key rotate and key copy), for an Aspire AppHost that reads the tunnel from parameters:

options.name: --project
options.description: The AppHost's .csproj. Writes Parameters:groundhog-tunnel-name (the tunnel name)

options.name: --name-parameter
options.description: Use Parameters:<name> for the tunnel name instead of groundhog-tunnel-name.

options.name: --key-parameter
options.description:
Use Parameters:<name> for the connection key instead of groundhog-tunnel-key.
Exit codes: 0 stopped (Ctrl+C), 1 other failure, 2 bad arguments, 3 key rejected or unknown tunnel.

options.name: --min-duration
options.description:
Saved profiles remember a tunnel name, its local target and its visitor access options, so
host <profile> and start <profile> need no other options. Profiles never store connection keys
or API keys (only --api-key-env names); the connection key comes from GROUNDHOG_KEY, --key, or
the key saved when you created the tunnel, added a key or rotated it here.
host, start, restart and init find groundhog.json in this directory or a parent.
Explicit options override the same-name saved profile, which overrides the project file.
Status and traffic commands describe local sessions; history retains the last 1,000 requests.

Options for host:
<name>           The tunnel's name, for example myapp.

options.name: --port
options.description: The local port to forward to (http://localhost:<port>).

options.name: --target
options.description: An HTTP or HTTPS local target, for example https://localhost:7132.

options.name: --local-ca
options.description: --insecure-local Skip local certificate validation for loopback HTTPS only (unsafe).

options.name: --key
options.description:
The tunnel's connection key. Prefer the GROUNDHOG_KEY environment variable,
which keeps the key out of your shell history and process list.

options.name: --pool
options.description: Connections to keep open to the relay, 1 to 8 (default 2).

options.name: --verbose
options.description:
Print one line per request.
